Technical 
 Bulletin
Title:
Boiler Problems Caused by Water
On-Stream Scale Removers ( OSSR )
Using kurtta Handbook of Water, P 2-42
Introduction

This 
document covers internal boiler water 
treatment even if the external boiler water treatment is employed, it is 
difficult to perfectly prevent the boiler water contamination with substances 
which cause the corrosion and scale problems. Boiler water treatment chemicals 
are used for protecting whole boiler systems including the feedwater and the 
steam condensate line from those problems. Antifoaming agents prevention of foaming of 
boiler water for preventing carryover problems.

This document was initiated 
by 
 EDEPC inspection & 
quality control chemist: Saad Sadeek; and revised 
by EEHC, Quality Control head Sector chemists: Mohamed Tawfik and Safaa Mamdouh.

This document is approved by eng. Samir Abd El-Galil: EDEPC 
 inspection and quality control general director & MPIS coordinator, 
 and certified by accountant; Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman; EDEPC admin and 
 financial inspection, quality control general director and supervisor of 
 inspection and quality control head sector.
Information

On-stream scale removers (OSSR) is a chemical which removes scale deposited 
in a boiler during the operation without the stoppage.

Scale is composed of several substances, such 
as calcium carbonate (CaCO3), calcium silicate (CaSiO3), 
hydroxiapatite ([Ca3(PO4)2]3Ca(OH)2), iron 
oxides (Fe2O3, Fe3O4) and zinc oxide 
(ZnO). The thermal conductivities of scales are quite small as shown in Table1. Therefore, even a small amount of scale adhesion reduces the boiler 
efficiency and increases the fuel consumption.

Heavy scale formation in the evaporation tubes 
will cause the expansion and bursting. To solve those scale troubles, the 
adhered scale has to be removed.

Table 1 Thermal conductivities of scale 
 components and metals

To remove scale, chemical cleaning or 
mechanical cleaning is generally carried out. However, the boiler has to be 
stopped for the cleaning. If it is possible to remove the scale from the boiler 
during the operation, it will realize a considerable energy saving. Previously, 
chelating agents were used as the OSSR, but their performances for scale removing were insufficient. Recently, the 
combined treatment of a low molecular weight polymer and a chelating agent has 
been developed and it has shown the excellent effect as the OSSR.

Figure 1 shows the increase in the total 
hardness of boiler water when the OSSR is applied for a fire and flue-tube 
boiler with the scale of calcium silicate mainly.

Figure 1 Increase of total hardness in boiler 
water by applying an OSSR

The sample A in Table 2 shows 
the composition of this scale. When the OSSR of 2,000 mg/l was injected 
into the boiler water, the total hardness was increased until 130 mg CaCO3/l by the scale removal. After 4 months, the excellent scale removal 
effects was determined by inspecting the boiler inside.
(Unit: %)
Table 2 Typical boiler scale analyses

The sample B in the Table 2 is a typical zinc base scale caused by a boiler 
water contamination with zinc coming from a condensate line made of 
galvanized steel.

Figure 2 shows the increase of zinc concentration in the boiler water by 
applying the OSSR. The excellent scale removal effect was observed when the 
boiler was inspected 3 months later.

Figure 2 Increase of total zinc in boiler water 
by applying an OSSR

Antifoaming 
Agents

Antifoaming agents prevent the carryover 
problems of boilers by controlling a foaming caused by the increase of dissolved 
or suspended solid concentration in the boiler water, or by the contamination of 
boiler water with oils, fats and organic matters.

Castor oil and cottonseed oil were used as 
antifoaming agents in the past. However, as their effects were insufficient and 
sometimes promoted the foaming, they are not used presently. At present, some 
kinds of amines, alcohols, fatty acid esters and so on are used as the 
antifoaming agents. These chemicals show the excellent effects with their small dosages.

Figure 3 shows a typical application result 
of an antifoaming agent. The high cycle number operation of boilers is realized 
without the carryover by applying the antifoaming agents.

Figure
